+# Glossary: Loa framework
+
+The shared language of the Loa agent framework, for humans and agents. It is mounted into every project with the framework and defines what each word means in day-to-day work; the mythic background of the names lives in the lore, and a project's own terms belong in that project's root glossary, never here.
+
+## Language
+
+**Beads**: The local-first task tracker that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
+_Aliases_: br
+
+**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
+
+**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
+
+**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
+
+**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
+
+**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
+_Avoid_: ADR, decision note
+
+**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
+_Avoid_: question task
+
+**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
+
+**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
+
+**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
+
+**decision:unblock**: The label of a decision ticket that a read-only probe settles by showing whether a suspected blocker is real; it never builds anything.
+
+**Dissent**: A second model's independent review of the same diff, triaged before a gate verdict.
+_Avoid_: second opinion, cross-check
+
+**Flatline**: The multi-model adversarial review of planning documents, in which independent voices review and cross-score each other before findings are integrated.
+_Aliases_: Flatline Protocol
+
+**Fog of war**: Decisions an effort can tell are coming but cannot yet phrase sharply; a map keeps them under Not yet specified.
+
+**Frontier**: The open, unblocked, unclaimed decision tickets of a map; in an interview, the questions whose prerequisites are already settled.
+
+**Golden path**: The five everyday commands (loa, plan, build, review and ship) that detect where the workflow stands and route to the right truename.
+
+**Grimoire**: The project's state area of planning documents, notes, reviews and records that agents read and write across sessions.
+
+**ICE**: Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics, the git safety layer of run mode that owns branch creation, push decisions and the refusal to touch protected branches.
+
+**Implement gate**: The hook that asks before an edit to application code made outside the implement or bug workflows.
+
+**Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
+_Aliases_: jack out
+
+**Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
+_Avoid_: converged
+
+**Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
+
+**Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
+_Aliases_: KF
+
+**Lore**: The mythic and narrative background of the framework's names, kept apart from this glossary, which defines only working meanings.
+
+**Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
+
+**Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
+
+**Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
+_Aliases_: RUNNING, HALTED, JACKED_OUT
+
+**Seam**: A point where a test observes the system, declared in a sprint plan together with what it catches, what it misses and its prior art.
+
+**Spike**: A throwaway prototype on its own branch that answers one decision ticket; only its report and its verdict row reach the working branch.
+
+**Truename**: The underlying command that a golden-path command routes to, used directly by power users.
+
+**Verdict trailer**: The machine-readable last line of a review or audit feedback document, which must agree with its findings. Any critical or high finding forces a changes-required verdict.
+_Aliases_: LOA-VERDICT
+
+**Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
+
+**Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

+++ b/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,346 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# red-test-check.sh: verify a bug fix's red-before-green (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2).
+#
+# A /bug micro-sprint commits its failing test alone ("Red commit: <sha>" in reviewer.md) before
+# the fix. This check runs the test command at the red commit and at the green revision, each in
+# its own detached worktree under `mktemp -d`, and reports whether the test failed before and
+# passes after:
+#
+#   0 VERIFIED     red fails by assertion and green passes
+#   1 GREEN_FAILS  green fails (red failed by assertion)
+#   2              usage error, a commit that does not resolve, red not a strict ancestor of
+#                  green, a worktree that cannot be created, or a failing --setup
+#   3 DECOY        the test passes at the red commit
+#   4 NOT_A_RED    --test-file absent at the red commit, or the red run failed for a
+#                  non-assertion reason (collection, compile, import, command not found)
+#   5 TIMEOUT      a run exceeded --timeout
+# The red-side verdicts (5, 3, 4) are judged first, then the green side (5, 1).
+#
+# Honest scope (as validate-ac-verification.sh states for its own check): this proves the
+# command failed before and passes after. It does not prove the assertion is right, that the
+# test exercises the bug, or that the fix is the cause; the reviewer still reads the test. The
+# not-a-red patterns are heuristics over the red run's output: a test whose own assertion
+# output contains one of them reads as NOT_A_RED (a false negative the reviewer can overrule).
+#
+# What runs where: the test argv runs with cwd = each worktree, never through `bash -c`.
+# Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts and nothing is stashed. Present dependency
+# directories (node_modules .venv vendor target .tox) are symlinked from the live tree into a
+# worktree that lacks them (--no-link-deps turns this off); a test that writes into a linked
+# directory writes into the live tree's copy. --setup is split on whitespace into an argv (no
+# shell syntax; point it at a script for anything more) and runs in each worktree first.
+# The timeout uses `timeout`, else `gtimeout`, else a bash watcher (TERM, then KILL after 2 s,
+# to the run's process group); with `timeout`/`gtimeout` a test that itself exits 124 reads as
+# a timeout. One cleanup removes both worktrees (worktree remove --force, then prune) and the
+# scratch directory on every exit path, interrupts included.
+#
+# Usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>]
+#                          [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>
+# Run it from inside the repository's work tree. --json prints one object on stdout:
+#   {red, green, red_exit, green_exit, verdict, red_tail, green_tail, linked_deps}
+# (the exits are null when a run did not happen). Exit 2 errors print to stderr only.
+# =============================================================================
+export LC_ALL=C
+set -euo pipefail
+
+PROG="red-test-check"
+DEP_DIRS="node_modules .venv vendor target .tox"
+TAIL_LINES=80
+
+# Not-a-red output patterns (ERE, matched on the red run's output when it failed). One entry
+# per runner; extend here, never inline.
+NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS=(
+  # bats: the file did not load (gather failure), a parse error, a missing file or command
+  'not ok [0-9]+ bats-gather-tests'
+  'syntax error near unexpected token'
+  'syntax error: unexpected end of file'
+  'Test file .* does not exist'
+  'command not found'
+  ': not found$'
+  # pytest: collection and import errors
+  'ERROR collecting'
+  'ImportError while importing'
+  # node (node:test, jest, mocha): an unresolved import or a parse error
+  'Cannot find module'
+  'SyntaxError'
+  # cargo: the crate or its tests did not build
+  'could not compile'
+  # go (1.22 toolchain): build or setup failure of the test binary
+  'build failed'
+  '\[setup failed\]'
+)
+
+usage(){
+  echo "${PROG}: $*" >&2
+  echo "usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>] [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+die2(){ echo "${PROG}: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+strip(){ tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177'; }
+
+RED=""
+GREEN="HEAD"
+TEST_FILE=""
+SETUP=""
+LINK_DEPS=1
+TIMEOUT=600
+JSON=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --red) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--red needs a commit"; RED="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --green) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--green needs a revision"; GREEN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --test-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--test-file needs a path"; TEST_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --setup) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--setup needs a command"; SETUP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --no-link-deps) LINK_DEPS=0; shift ;;
+    --timeout) [[ "${2:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,4}$ ]] || usage "--timeout needs seconds (1-99999)"; TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --) shift; break ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '3,41p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) usage "unknown argument '$1' (the test command goes after --)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+[[ -n "$RED" ]] || usage "--red is required"
+[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage "a test command is required after --"
+case "$RED" in -*) usage "--red must be a commit, not an option" ;; esac
+case "$GREEN" in -*) usage "--green must be a revision, not an option" ;; esac
+case "$TEST_FILE" in
+  /*) usage "--test-file must be relative to the repository root" ;;
+  -*) usage "--test-file must be a path, not an option" ;;
+esac
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]] && ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then die2 "--json needs jq"; fi
+SETUP_ARGV=()
+if [[ -n "$SETUP" ]]; then
+  read -r -a SETUP_ARGV <<< "$SETUP"
+  [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]] || usage "--setup is empty"
+fi
+
+MAIN="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree"
+MAIN="$(cd "$MAIN" && pwd -P)"
+
+RED_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RED}^{commit}")" || die2 "--red '${RED}' does not resolve to a commit"
+GREEN_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${GREEN}^{commit}")" || die2 "--green '${GREEN}' does not resolve to a commit"
+if [[ "$RED_SHA" == "$GREEN_SHA" ]] || ! git -C "$MAIN" merge-base --is-ancestor "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA"; then
+  die2 "red ${RED_SHA} is not a strict ancestor of green ${GREEN_SHA}: commit the failing test first, then the fix"
+fi
+
+RED_EXIT=""
+GREEN_EXIT=""
+RED_TAIL=""
+GREEN_TAIL=""
+LINKED=""
+
+# Report a verdict (text or JSON) and exit with its code.
+finish(){
+  local verdict="$1" code="$2"
+  if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    jq -n --arg red "$RED_SHA" --arg green "$GREEN_SHA" --arg re "$RED_EXIT" --arg ge "$GREEN_EXIT" \
+      --arg verdict "$verdict" --arg rt "$RED_TAIL" --arg gt "$GREEN_TAIL" --arg linked "$LINKED" \
+      '{red: $red, green: $green,
+        red_exit: (if $re == "" then null else ($re | tonumber) end),
+        green_exit: (if $ge == "" then null else ($ge | tonumber) end),
+        verdict: $verdict, red_tail: $rt, green_tail: $gt,
+        linked_deps: ($linked | split(" ") | map(select(. != "")))}'
+    if [[ -n "$RED_TAIL" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL" >&2
+    fi
+  else
+    echo "${PROG}: red ${RED_SHA} exit ${RED_EXIT:-n/a}; green ${GREEN_SHA} exit ${GREEN_EXIT:-n/a}; linked deps: ${LINKED:-none}"
+    if [[ -n "$RED_EXIT" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL"
+    fi
+    if [[ -n "$GREEN_EXIT" && "$GREEN_EXIT" != "0" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- green run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end green run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$GREEN_TAIL"
+    fi
+    echo "verdict: ${verdict}"
+  fi
+  exit "$code"
+}
+
+# D-7.6: the named test file must exist at the red commit.
+if [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" ]] && ! git -C "$MAIN" cat-file -e "${RED_SHA}:${TEST_FILE#./}" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "${PROG}: --test-file '${TEST_FILE}' does not exist at the red commit ${RED_SHA}: the failing test was not committed there" >&2
+  finish NOT_A_RED 4
+fi
+
+# WARN: a green that differs from red only in test files cannot be a fix.
+is_test_path(){
+  local p="$1" b
+  b="${p##*/}"

+  return 1
+}

+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue

+done < <(git -C "$MAIN" diff --name-only "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA" -- 2>/dev/null || true)

+  echo "${PROG}: WARN: no non-test file changed between red ${RED_SHA} and green ${GREEN_SHA}; a pass there comes from test changes alone" >&2

+SCRATCH="$(cd "$SCRATCH" && pwd -P)"
+WT_RED=""
+WT_GREEN=""
+RUN_PID=""
+WATCH_PID=""
+remove_wt(){
+  local wt="$1" d
+  [[ -n "$wt" ]] || return 0

+  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
+    if [[ -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then rm -f -- "${wt}/${d}"; fi
+  done

+}
+cleanup(){
+  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
+  if [[ -n "$RUN_PID" ]]; then
+    kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  remove_wt "$WT_RED"
+  remove_wt "$WT_GREEN"

+trap 'exit 143' TERM

+add_wt(){

+link_deps(){

+RUN_TIMED_OUT=0

+  local cwd="$1" log="$2" flag="${SCRATCH}/timed-out" tbin="" start

+  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=timeout
+  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=gtimeout
+  fi
+  start=$SECONDS

+  # whole tree it spawned.
+  set -m
+  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
+    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$tbin" -k 2 "$TIMEOUT" "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
+  else
+    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
+  fi

+  set +m
+  if [[ -z "$tbin" ]]; then

+      while kill -0 "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null; do

+          : > "$flag"
+          kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+          sleep 2
+          kill -KILL -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        sleep 1
+        i=$((i + 1))
+      done ) < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &
+    WATCH_PID=$!
+  fi
+  set +e
+  wait "$RUN_PID"
+  RUN_RC=$?
+  set -e
+  RUN_PID=""
+  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then
+    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    WATCH_PID=""
+  fi
+  RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
+  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
+    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 124 ]] || { [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 137 ]] && [[ $((SECONDS - start)) -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; }; then RUN_TIMED_OUT=1; fi
+  elif [[ -f "$flag" ]]; then
+    RUN_TIMED_OUT=1
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+prepare(){
+  local wt="$1" name="$2"
+  link_deps "$wt"
+  if [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
+    run_bounded "$wt" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" "${SETUP_ARGV[@]}"
+    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -ne 0 || "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+      tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" | strip >&2
+      if [[ "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then die2 "--setup timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s in the ${name} worktree"; fi
+      die2 "--setup exited ${RUN_RC} in the ${name} worktree"
+    fi
+  fi
+}
+
+WT_RED="${SCRATCH}/red"
+add_wt "$WT_RED" "$RED_SHA"
+WT_GREEN="${SCRATCH}/green"
+add_wt "$WT_GREEN" "$GREEN_SHA"
+prepare "$WT_RED" red
+prepare "$WT_GREEN" green
+
+run_bounded "$WT_RED" "${SCRATCH}/red.log" "$@"
+RED_EXIT="$RUN_RC"
+RED_TO="$RUN_TIMED_OUT"
+RED_TAIL="$(tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/red.log" | strip)"
+
+run_bounded "$WT_GREEN" "${SCRATCH}/green.log" "$@"
+GREEN_EXIT="$RUN_RC"
+GREEN_TO="$RUN_TIMED_OUT"
+GREEN_TAIL="$(tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/green.log" | strip)"
+
+if [[ "$RED_TO" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: the red run exceeded ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
+  finish TIMEOUT 5
+fi
+if [[ "$RED_EXIT" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug" >&2
+  finish DECOY 3
+fi
+if [[ "$RED_EXIT" -eq 126 || "$RED_EXIT" -eq 127 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: the red run exited ${RED_EXIT} (command not found or not executable): not an assertion failure" >&2
+  finish NOT_A_RED 4
+fi
+# Strip once into a file: `strip | grep -q` under pipefail can turn a match into a miss.
+strip < "${SCRATCH}/red.log" > "${SCRATCH}/red.clean"
+for pat in "${NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
+  if grep -qE -- "$pat" "${SCRATCH}/red.clean"; then
+    echo "${PROG}: the red run failed by a non-assertion error (matched '${pat}'): fix the test so it loads, then re-check" >&2
+    finish NOT_A_RED 4
+  fi
+done
+if [[ "$GREEN_TO" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: the green run exceeded ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
+  finish TIMEOUT 5
+fi
+if [[ "$GREEN_EXIT" -ne 0 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: the test still fails at green ${GREEN_SHA}" >&2
+  finish GREEN_FAILS 1
+fi
+finish VERIFIED 0

+name: Glossary Terms
+
+# cycle-128 FR-6 (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, D-6.3): every backticked framework
+# term in the kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) resolves to an entry or alias in
+# the framework glossary (.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md), or to an allowlisted code
+# identifier (.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt, at most 30 entries).
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh is the gate; the two control steps prove the
+# gate itself still bites. This check is Loa's own: it runs in this repository
+# only, never in a project that mounts the framework.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+
+jobs:
+  glossary-terms:
+    name: Kernel terms resolve to the glossary
+    if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
+        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
+
+      - name: Check kernel terms against the glossary
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file GLOSSARY.md
+
+      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the miss fixture with exit 1)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/miss
+          rc=0
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt" || rc=$?
+          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh did not reject $d with exit 1 (got $rc)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: miss fixture rejected"
+
+      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the ok fixture)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/ok
+          if ! bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt"; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh false-positive on $d"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: ok fixture accepted"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# red-test-check.sh: verify a bug fix's red-before-green (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2).
     4	#
     5	# A /bug micro-sprint commits its failing test alone ("Red commit: <sha>" in reviewer.md) before
     6	# the fix. This check runs the test command at the red commit and at the green revision, each in
     7	# its own detached worktree under `mktemp -d`, and reports whether the test failed before and
     8	# passes after:
     9	#
    10	#   0 VERIFIED     red fails by assertion and green passes
    11	#   1 GREEN_FAILS  green fails (red failed by assertion)
    12	#   2              usage error, a commit that does not resolve, red not a strict ancestor of
    13	#                  green, a worktree that cannot be created, or a failing --setup
    14	#   3 DECOY        the test passes at the red commit
    15	#   4 NOT_A_RED    --test-file absent at the red commit, or the red run failed for a
    16	#                  non-assertion reason (collection, compile, import, command not found)
    17	#   5 TIMEOUT      a run exceeded --timeout
    18	# The red-side verdicts (5, 3, 4) are judged first, then the green side (5, 1).
    19	#
    20	# Honest scope (as validate-ac-verification.sh states for its own check): this proves the
    21	# command failed before and passes after. It does not prove the assertion is right, that the
    22	# test exercises the bug, or that the fix is the cause; the reviewer still reads the test. The
    23	# not-a-red patterns are heuristics over the red run's output: a test whose own assertion
    24	# output contains one of them reads as NOT_A_RED (a false negative the reviewer can overrule).
    25	#
    26	# What runs where: the test argv runs with cwd = each worktree, never through `bash -c`.
    27	# Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts and nothing is stashed. Present dependency
    28	# directories (node_modules .venv vendor target .tox) are symlinked from the live tree into a

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
     4	# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
     5	#
     6	# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
     7	# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
     8	# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
     9	# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
    10	# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
    11	# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
    12	# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
    13	# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
    14	# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
    15	# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
    16	#
    17	# Usage:
    18	#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
    19	#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
    20	#
    21	#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
    22	#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
    23	#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
    24	#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
    25	#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
    26	#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
    27	#
    28	# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
    29	#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
    30	#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    36	
    37	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    38	KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    39	GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    40	ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
    41	ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
    42	JSON=0
    43	REPORT=0
    44	ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
    45	
    46	need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
    47	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    50	    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    51	    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    52	    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
    53	    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
    54	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    55	    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    56	  esac
    57	done
    58	
    59	for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
    60	  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
    61	done
    62	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
    63	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
    64	fi
    65	
    66	# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
    67	rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
    68	DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
    69	
    70	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
    71	trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
    72	
    73	# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
    74	awk '
    75	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    76	  fence { next }
    77	  {
    78	    s = $0
    79	    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
    80	      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
    81	      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
    82	      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
    83	    }
    84	  }
    85	' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
    86	
    87	# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
    88	#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
    89	awk '
    90	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    91	  fence { next }
    92	  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
    93	  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
    94	  !lang { next }
    95	  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
    96	    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
    97	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
    98	    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
    99	  }
   100	  /^_Aliases_:/ {
   101	    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
   102	    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
   103	    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   104	      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
   105	      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
   106	    }
   107	  }
   108	' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
   109	
   110	# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
   111	awk '
   112	  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
   113	    if (s == "") next
   114	    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
   115	' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
   116	
   117	# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
   118	#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
   119	#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
   120	#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
   121	#    glossary already resolves.
   122	awk -F'\t' '
   123	  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
   124	  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
   125	  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
   126	  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
   127	  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
   128	                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
   129	                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
   130	  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
   131	  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
   132	  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
   133	  {
   134	    used[norm($2)] = 1
   135	    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
   136	    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
   137	    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
   138	    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
   139	    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
   140	  }
   141	  END {
   142	    for (k in allow) {
   143	      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
   144	      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
   145	        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
   146	    }
   147	  }
   148	' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   149	
   150	kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   151	allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   152	n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
   153	n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
   154	
   155	violations=()
   156	warnings=()
   157	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
   158	  case "$r" in
   159	    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
   160	    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
   161	    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
   162	  esac
   163	done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   164	if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
   165	  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
   166	fi
   167	
   168	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   169	  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
   170	     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
   171	     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
   172	     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
   173	    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
   174	    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
   175	    | {ok: null,
   176	       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
   177	       kept: ($tokens | length),

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
     4	# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
     5	#
     6	# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
     7	# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
     8	# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
     9	# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
    10	# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
    11	# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
    12	# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
    13	# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
    14	# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
    15	# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
    16	#
    17	# Usage:
    18	#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
    19	#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
    20	#
    21	#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
    22	#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
    23	#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
    24	#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
    25	#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
    26	#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
    27	#
    28	# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
    29	#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
    30	#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    36	
    37	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    38	KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    39	GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    40	ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
    41	ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
    42	JSON=0
    43	REPORT=0
    44	ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
    45	
    46	need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
    47	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    50	    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    51	    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    52	    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
    53	    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
    54	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    55	    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    56	  esac
    57	done
    58	
    59	for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
    60	  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
    61	done
    62	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
    63	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
    64	fi
    65	
    66	# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
    67	rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
    68	DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
    69	
    70	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
    71	trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
    72	
    73	# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
    74	awk '
    75	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    76	  fence { next }
    77	  {
    78	    s = $0
    79	    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
    80	      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
    81	      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
    82	      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
    83	    }
    84	  }
    85	' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
    86	
    87	# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
    88	#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
    89	awk '
    90	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    91	  fence { next }
    92	  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
    93	  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
    94	  !lang { next }
    95	  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
    96	    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
    97	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
    98	    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
    99	  }
   100	  /^_Aliases_:/ {
   101	    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
   102	    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
   103	    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   104	      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
   105	      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
   106	    }
   107	  }
   108	' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
   109	
   110	# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
   111	awk '
   112	  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
   113	    if (s == "") next
   114	    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
   115	' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
   116	
   117	# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
   118	#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
   119	#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
   120	#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
   121	#    glossary already resolves.
   122	awk -F'\t' '
   123	  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
   124	  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
   125	  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
   126	  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
   127	  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
   128	                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
   129	                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
   130	  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
   131	  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
   132	  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
   133	  {
   134	    used[norm($2)] = 1
   135	    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
   136	    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
   137	    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
   138	    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
   139	    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
   140	  }
   141	  END {
   142	    for (k in allow) {
   143	      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
   144	      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
   145	        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
   146	    }
   147	  }
   148	' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   149	
   150	kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   151	allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   152	n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
   153	n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
   154	
   155	violations=()
   156	warnings=()
   157	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
   158	  case "$r" in
   159	    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
   160	    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
   161	    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
   162	  esac
   163	done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   164	if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
   165	  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
   166	fi
   167	
   168	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   169	  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
   170	     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
   171	     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
   172	     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
   173	    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
   174	    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
   175	    | {ok: null,
   176	       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
   177	       kept: ($tokens | length),
   178	       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
   179	                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
   180	                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
   181	                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
   182	       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
   183	       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
   184	       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
   185	       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
   186	       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
   187	       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
   188	       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
   189	    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
   190	  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   191	else
   192	  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
   193	    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
   194	      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   195	  fi
   196	  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
   197	  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
   198	  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
   199	  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
   200	fi
   201	
   202	[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
   203	exit 0

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
     3	# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
     4	# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
     5	
     6	setup() {
     7	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
     8	    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
     9	    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
    10	    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
    11	    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
    12	    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    13	    git -C "$R" init -q
    14	    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
    15	    git -C "$R" config user.name t
    16	    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
    17	    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
    18	    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
    19	    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
    20	    commit "base"
    21	}
    22	
    23	commit() { git -C "$R" add -A && git -C "$R" commit -q -m "$1"; git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD; }
    24	
    25	# The red test: asserts add 2 3 = 5 and prints what it got.
    26	add_red_test() {
    27	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
    28	    cat > "$R/tests/test_add.sh" <<'EOF'
    29	. ./lib.sh
    30	got="$(add 2 3)"
    31	if [ "$got" = 5 ]; then echo "PASS add"; exit 0; fi
    32	echo "FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got $got"
    33	exit 1
    34	EOF
    35	}
    36	fix_lib() { printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 + $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"; }
    37	
    38	# Status of the fixture after a run: only the main tree, no stash, the live tree as it was.
    39	assert_clean() {
    40	    local n
    41	    n="$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    42	    [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || { git -C "$R" worktree list; echo "worktrees left behind"; return 1; }
    43	    [ -z "$(git -C "$R" stash list)" ] || { echo "a stash was created"; return 1; }
    44	    [ -z "$(ls -A "$TMPDIR")" ] || { ls -la "$TMPDIR"; echo "scratch left behind"; return 1; }
    45	}
    46	
    47	rtc() { (cd "$R" && "$SCRIPT" "$@"); }
    48	
    49	@test "RTC-1 red fails by assertion, green passes: exit 0 VERIFIED with the red output printed" {
    50	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
    51	    fix_lib; commit "fix(bug): add adds" >/dev/null
    52	    run rtc --red "$red" --test-file tests/test_add.sh -- sh tests/test_add.sh
    53	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    54	    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: VERIFIED"* ]]
    55	    [[ "$output" == *"--- red run (last 80 lines) ---"*"FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got -1"*"--- end red run ---"* ]]
    56	    [[ "$output" != *"WARN: no non-test file changed"* ]]
    57	    assert_clean
    58	}
    59	
    60	@test "RTC-2 a decoy that passes at both commits exits 3 DECOY" {
    61	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'echo "PASS always"\nexit 0\n' > "$R/tests/test_decoy.sh"
    62	    red="$(commit "test: decoy")"
    63	    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
    64	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_decoy.sh
    65	    [ "$status" -eq 3 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    66	    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: DECOY"* ]]
    67	    [[ "$output" == *"PASS always"* ]]
    68	    assert_clean
    69	}
    70	
    71	@test "RTC-3 a --test-file absent at the red commit exits 4 NOT_A_RED before any worktree" {
    72	    printf 'x\n' > "$R/README"; red="$(commit "docs")"

1	# Glossary: Loa framework
     2	
     3	The shared language of the Loa agent framework, for humans and agents. It is mounted into every project with the framework and defines what each word means in day-to-day work; the mythic background of the names lives in the lore, and a project's own terms belong in that project's root glossary, never here.
     4	
     5	## Language
     6	
     7	**Beads**: The local-first task tracker that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
     8	_Aliases_: br
     9	
    10	**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
    11	
    12	**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
    13	
    14	**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
    15	
    16	**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
    17	
    18	**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
    19	_Avoid_: ADR, decision note
    20	
    21	**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
    22	_Avoid_: question task
    23	
    24	**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
    25	
    26	**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
    27	
    28	**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
    29

# === Update .gitignore for Submodule Mode (Task 1.6) ===
update_gitignore_for_submodule() {
  step "Updating .gitignore for submodule mode..."

  local gitignore=".gitignore"
  touch "$gitignore"

  # Symlink entries — these are created by mount-submodule.sh and should not be tracked
  local symlink_entries=(
    ".claude/scripts"
    ".claude/protocols"
    ".claude/hooks"
    ".claude/data"
    ".claude/schemas"
    ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ".claude/loa/reference"
    ".claude/loa/feedback-ontology.yaml"
    ".claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    ".claude/loa/learnings"
    ".claude/settings.json"
    ".claude/checksums.json"
    # cycle-115: real files generated by the pinned Aleph installer.
    ".claude/aleph"
    ".claude/commands/loa-aleph.md"
    ".claude/skills/loa-aleph"
  )

  # State and backup entries (not symlinks but must be gitignored)
  local state_entries=(
    ".loa-state/"
    ".claude.backup.*"
    # cycle-115: the transactional Aleph installer may leave these exact
    # recovery/coordination names after interruption.
    ".claude/aleph-install.transaction*"
    ".claude/aleph-install.writer.lock*"
  )

  # Add header if not present
  if ! grep -q "LOA SUBMODULE SYMLINKS" "$gitignore" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "" >> "$gitignore"
----
  # Both are framework-managed (System Zone) directories that map 1:1 to
  # the submodule, same as scripts / protocols / data / schemas.
  #
  # #842: `.claude/hooks` is DELIBERATELY excluded from the symlink set and
  # listed in MANIFEST_COPY_DIRS instead. Claude Code's hook executor on
  # macOS cannot follow relative symlinks like `.claude/hooks ->
  # ../.loa/.claude/hooks` from a subprocess context — every hook fails
  # silently with "No such file or directory". Copying is the only fix
  # that doesn't require changes to Claude Code itself.
  MANIFEST_DIR_SYMLINKS=(
    ".claude/scripts:../${submodule}/.claude/scripts"
    ".claude/protocols:../${submodule}/.claude/protocols"
    ".claude/data:../${submodule}/.claude/data"
    ".claude/schemas:../${submodule}/.claude/schemas"
    ".claude/adapters:../${submodule}/.claude/adapters"
    ".claude/defaults:../${submodule}/.claude/defaults"
  )

  # #842: items COPIED into the consumer tree instead of symlinked.
  # Required for files/dirs that Claude Code (or other subprocess-spawned
  # executors) reads/exec'd at runtime, where relative-symlink resolution
  # through `..` traversal fails on macOS. Tradeoff: after `git submodule
  # update --remote`, operators must re-run `mount-submodule.sh --force`
  # to pick up changes in these paths. The cost is small (~20 files) and
  # explicit (mount has to run on every submodule bump anyway).
  MANIFEST_COPY_DIRS=(
    ".claude/hooks:${submodule}/.claude/hooks"
  )

  MANIFEST_COPY_FILES=(
    ".claude/settings.json:${submodule}/.claude/settings.json"
  )

  # Phase 2: File and nested symlinks (deeper paths with 2-level relative targets)
  MANIFEST_FILE_SYMLINKS=(
    ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ".claude/loa/reference:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/reference"
    ".claude/loa/learnings:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/learnings"
    ".claude/loa/feedback-ontology.yaml:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/feedback-ontology.yaml"
    ".claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    ".claude/checksums.json:../${submodule}/.claude/checksums.json"
  )

  # Phase 3: Per-skill symlinks (dynamic — discovered from submodule content)
  MANIFEST_SKILL_SYMLINKS=()
  if [[ -d "${repo_root}/${submodule}/.claude/skills" ]]; then
    for skill_dir in "${repo_root}/${submodule}"/.claude/skills/*/; do
      if [[ -d "$skill_dir" ]]; then
        local skill_name
        skill_name=$(basename "$skill_dir")
        # cycle-115: receipt-managed by the pinned Aleph installer. This must be
        # a real directory in the consumer tree, never a submodule symlink.
        [[ "$skill_name" == "loa-aleph" ]] && continue
        MANIFEST_SKILL_SYMLINKS+=(".claude/skills/${skill_name}:../../${submodule}/.claude/skills/${skill_name}")
      fi
    done
  fi

  # Phase 4: Per-command symlinks (dynamic — discovered from submodule content)
  MANIFEST_CMD_SYMLINKS=()
  if [[ -d "${repo_root}/${submodule}/.claude/commands" ]]; then
    for cmd_file in "${repo_root}/${submodule}"/.claude/commands/*.md; do
      if [[ -f "$cmd_file" ]]; then
        local cmd_name
        cmd_name=$(basename "$cmd_file")
        # cycle-115: receipt-managed by the pinned Aleph installer. This must be
        # a real file in the consumer tree, never a submodule symlink.
        [[ "$cmd_name" == "loa-aleph.md" ]] && continue
        MANIFEST_CMD_SYMLINKS+=(".claude/commands/${cmd_name}:../../${submodule}/.claude/commands/${cmd_name}")
      fi
    done

head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52 — The NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS list has no pattern for a test file that is missing at the red commit when the runner is not bats or node. Examples: `sh: 0: cannot open tests/t.sh: No such file` from dash/sh, and pytest's `ERROR: file or directory not found` (exit 4). Reproduced: commit test and fix together, pass the pre-test commit as `--red`, run `-- sh tests/t.sh`. The red run exits 2 with "cannot open", that counts as an assertion failure, and the script prints `verdict: VERIFIED` and exits 0. This is the exact case the red-before-green discipline is meant to reject. Only `--test-file` catches it, and none of the documented invocations pass that flag.
head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43 — This criterion says a 0 exit from `red-test-check.sh` proves the fix "does not weaken the test". It does not. When green only rewrites the test, the script still exits 0 VERIFIED and prints only a stderr WARN (RTC-14 asserts exactly that), and it has no weakening check at all once any non-test file also changes. The invocation also leaves out `--test-file {suggested_test_file}`, the only enforcement of D-7.6 ("committed alone"). Pass `--test-file`, and either make a test-only green fail or drop the "does not weaken the test" claim.
head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219 — The reviewer is told to run `red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit> -- <test command>` and cite its output as proof that 'Test fails with current code'. The command has no `--test-file`, so the test-absent-at-red check never runs and the false VERIFIED described above goes through. Nothing tells the reviewer to treat the "no non-test file changed" WARN as blocking, so a weakened-test VERIFIED gets cited as evidence.
head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6 — `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` here, plus `args: ["*"]` at line 28, lets the review skill run any argv after `--` and any `--setup` command. That turns a tightly scoped read-mostly tool allowlist into arbitrary command execution. The script also symlinks the live tree's node_modules/.venv/vendor/target/.tox into the worktrees, so the test command can write to them. Restrict the pattern (for example a fixed test-runner prefix, and no `--setup`), or record this as an explicit, accepted widening of the reviewer's permissions.
head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:241 — An unrelated compression dropped "regardless of other findings" from "**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED**". That phrase is what makes the AC-Verification failures override the "medium/low accumulation is your call" discretion in the paragraph above. Without it the rule is weaker and ambiguous. Restore it.
head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:204 — An unrelated rewording dropped the "A large sprint" trigger for the per-task parallel split. Only ">3 tasks" splits now, so a large sprint with few tasks no longer does. This behavior change is outside the PR's stated scope. Restore it, or justify it in the PR.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1263 — The comment says glossary names "compare as the drift check matches them", but the duplicate check never folds plurals, and check-glossary-terms.sh does (s/es, singular of a plural). `**Bead**` and `**Beads**` both pass the validator. The checker then resolves a kernel `beads` to the entry "Bead" (first match wins) rather than "Beads". Add the plural fold to `norm()`/`claim()` so a collision the checker would make is rejected.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:897 — The seams rule fails open in a validator documented as "fail-closed". A plan whose header Date is missing, left as the template's `{DATE}` placeholder, or written in a non-ISO form ("Oct 14, 2026") reads as undated and only WARNs. So the requirement disappears when the date is formatted differently. At least treat a header `**Date:**` line with no ISO date as a violation.
head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:16 — The new job has no `permissions:` block, so it inherits the repository's default GITHUB_TOKEN scope. It only reads the checkout. Declare `permissions: contents: read`, matching the pinned-action supply-chain hardening it already uses.

The review is in `/workspace/review.md` with nine findings. The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**: the new red-before-green check can report a pass when the test was never committed first, which is the case it exists to catch.

**How I checked it:** I ran all 66 new bats tests on a scratch copy outside `pr/`, and they pass. To get there I had to make the scripts executable, add an empty stand-in for `compat-lib.sh` (not in the PR), and download the kernel file `.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md` from the upstream GitHub repo's `main` branch. That copy may not match the PR's base exactly. I then reproduced the main defects by hand and deleted the scratch copy. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Blocking:**
- **`red-test-check.sh:52` gives a false pass.** I committed the test and the fix together and passed the commit before them as `--red`. With the test run as `sh tests/t.sh`, the red run fails with "cannot open … No such file", which the script counts as a real test failure, so it prints `VERIFIED` and exits 0. It has no pattern for that message from `sh`, or for pytest's "file or directory not found". Only `--test-file` catches this case.
- **Templates overstate what the check proves.** `micro-sprint.md:43` and `reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219` both run the check without `--test-file`. The micro-sprint template also says exit 0 proves the fix "does not weaken the test". It doesn't: the PR's own test RTC-14 shows the script exits 0 when the "fix" only rewrites the test, with just a warning.
- **The review skill gains arbitrary command execution.** `reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6` (and line 28) allows `red-test-check.sh` with any arguments. Whatever comes after `--`, and any `--setup` value, runs as a command, so the reviewer's narrow tool allowlist no longer limits anything. The linked dependency folders (such as `node_modules`) also point at the live tree, so tests can write into it.

**Lower severity:**
- **Unrelated wording cuts in `reviewing-code/SKILL.md` change behavior:**
  - Line 241 drops "regardless of other findings" from the automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED rule, which weakens it.
  - Line 204 drops the "large sprint" trigger for splitting review work per task.
- **Glossary duplicate check (`validate-artifact.sh:1263`) doesn't fold plurals the way the term checker does.** `Bead` and `Beads` both pass validation, and the checker then resolves `beads` to the wrong entry.
- **The new seams rule fails open (`validate-artifact.sh:897`).** A plan with no date, the template's `{DATE}` placeholder, or a non-ISO date only gets a warning.
- **The new workflow sets no `permissions:` block (`check-glossary-terms.yml:16`).** It should declare `contents: read`.
